statement: >= 2 of the top-3 compute jurisdictions publish new or expanded controls on AI chips, chip tools or model weights (official gazettes; calendar 2027)
status_at_phase_end: Resolves on calendar 2027; 2025 shows the base rate. Both leading jurisdictions published new or expanded controls in 2025: Bloc A (model-weight and chip framework in January, later rescinded; foundry due-diligence rule; 50%-affiliates rule in September) and Bloc B (October rare-earth controls with case-by-case review for advanced-chip and military-AI end uses). Late 2025 brought a partial truce: both sides suspended their autumn measures for one year from 10 Nov 2025, and Bloc A moved to allow sales of a more advanced chip to Bloc B in December. Pattern: controls are issued often, but are also traded away.

items.summary: Bloc A published an interim final rule revising controls on advanced computing chips worldwide (three-tier country framework) and adding the first export control on closed model weights of certain advanced AI models.
items.detail: BIS 'Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion', Federal Register 2025-00636 (2025-01-15); compliance date 2025-05-15. A companion foundry due-diligence rule was issued the same week.

items.summary: Bloc A's commerce ministry began rescinding the January diffusion/model-weights rule before it took effect, while issuing guidance that strengthens chip controls (e.g., on using a Bloc B firm's advanced accelerators anywhere, and diversion risks).
items.detail: BIS press release 2025-05-12: rescission of AI Diffusion Rule; guidance that using Huawei Ascend chips anywhere may violate the EAR; warnings on training Bloc B models with Bloc A chips. Mixed: removes weight control, adds chip guidance.

items.summary: Bloc A expanded end-user controls so that any entity >=50% owned by listed parties is automatically restricted (Affiliates Rule), widening chip and tool export restrictions to subsidiaries.
items.detail: BIS interim final rule 'Expansion of End-User Controls to Cover Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities', 90 FR 47201 (2025-09-30), effective 2025-09-29.

items.summary: Bloc B published extraterritorial rare-earth export controls (with a 50% rule) requiring case-by-case review of exports for R&D/production of logic chips at 14 nm and below, 256+-layer memory, related chip-making equipment and materials, and AI with potential military use.
items.detail: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 61 (and Nos. 56-62), 2025-10-09; Part 1(c) effective on issuance, extraterritorial parts planned for 2025-12-01. CSET translation verified via search snippet.

items.summary: After a bilateral trade truce, Bloc A suspended its Affiliates Rule for one year from 2025-11-10, and Bloc B suspended global implementation of its October export controls in exchange. Shows controls are negotiable and can be paused.
items.detail: BIS final rule 2025-19846 (FR 2025-11-12) staying the rule until 2026-11-09; Bloc B's reciprocal suspension of the Oct 9 measures (per Squire Patton Boggs).

items.summary: Bloc A's head of government said a more advanced accelerator could be sold to approved customers in Bloc B with a share of revenue to the government - a loosening of chip controls rather than a tightening.
items.detail: Trump announcement allowing Nvidia H200 exports to Bloc B with 25% to the Bloc A government (reported 2025-12-08). Not verified via web_extract this run.
